thread:
Maria: quick heads-up — noticed a ~15% drop in prefix cache hit-rate after yesterday's deploy (tokenizer v2). profiling shows a lot of keys miss because tokenization changed spacing/normalization. sample diff below and repro steps.

Maria: repro: `curl -X POST /v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-llama-13b","prompt":"Hello

System: use friendly tone"}'` -> cache miss. Old tokenizer produced different tokenization and different normalized prefix hash.

Maria: profiler snippet: `prefix_cache_hit_rate: 0.68 -> 0.53` on prod after deploy; kernel selection/batching unaffected. KV cache warmup percentile latency increased ~8ms for 95th.

Jon: :eyes: do we currently include tokenizer/version in the cache key?

Maria: no — key is currently `model:system_id:normalized_prompt` (we normalize whitespace but not tokenizer semantics). we also strip trailing spaces but don't canonicalize unicode variations.

Kevin: that explains it. tokenizer changes can change token boundaries even if visible text identical. we should include `tokenizer_version` in the key and maybe a short `prefix_hash` instead of raw prompt to keep key size down.

Sarah: agree. also we need to decide what to do about function/tool call fields — many clients include ephemeral meta (timestamps in tool args) which pollutes the key. we should canonicalize function calls: drop known-noise fields and sort args, maybe include a stable fingerprint for the call shape.

Maria: proposal: new cache-key template: `{{model}}:{{tokenizer_v}}:{{system_id}}:{{prefix_hash}}:{{call_shape_hash?}}` where `prefix_hash = sha1(normalize_text(prompt + system))[:16]`. normalization includes NFKC, collapse whitespace, strip non-semantic punctuation, and remove ephemeral keys from JSON args.

Jon: sounds good. two operational concerns: 1) rolling migration — when we add tokenizer_v, old keys miss so w/e warmed caches are invalid; 2) key explosion if we include full function args.

Kevin: for 1) we can do staged warmup: after deploy, sample top 5k prefixes from recent traffic, compute new keys using new template and pre-populate KV caches async. that will recover hit-rate fast. for 2) compute call_shape_hash = sha1(sorted_keys + truncated_values) to keep cardinality low.

Sarah: add a feature-flag for backward-compat fallback: if miss on new-key, fallback to old-key lookup for N seconds (and if hit, write new-key). avoids regression for a short time while caches warm up. we need metrics for fallback rate.

Maria: implemented a quick pilot in staging: `cache_key_version=2` with tokenizer_v included + call_shape hashing. results: hit-rate improved from 0.54 -> 0.73 after prewarm run. latency tail dropped ~6ms.

Maria: PR I'll open: `eng-runtime#4821` — includes normalization util, tokenizer version read from model metadata, and prewarm job (k8s cronjob) that samples hot prefixes from analytics. also adds `cache.fallback_window_sec` config default 600s.

Jon: please add a small doc blurb in `eng-runtime` runbook about how to compute call_shape allowlist and how to add new noisy fields.

Kevin: action items: Maria open PR, Sarah add fallback metric dashboard (cache.new_key_fallback_rate), Jon add runbook note, infra run prewarm once PR is merged.

deploy-bot: rolled out `tokenizer-v2` to prod yesterday at 03:12 UTC — leaving note of deploy in thread. :white_check_mark:

Maria: thanks — I'll tag folks on the PR and include sample prewarm command and a short script to compute top prefixes.

Sarah: :+1: def want telemetry on `fallback_rate` and `prewarm_coverage` before full rollout for other models.

Jon: if we pin tokenizer_version per-model in the model catalog we can more safely reason about migrations going forward. file a small change in cadence.

Kevin: ok let's ship the pilot next week after PR review. thanks all.
